response.sql:
WITH patient_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    ID,
    AVG(PIC) AS avg_pic,
    AVG(HGB) / AVG(HCT) AS ratio
  FROM Laboratory
  GROUP BY ID
),
overall_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio
  FROM patient_stats
),
above_avg_patients AS (
  SELECT avg_pic, ratio
  FROM patient_stats
  WHERE ratio > (SELECT avg_ratio FROM overall_avg)
)
SELECT 
  AVG(avg_pic) AS avg_pic,
  AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio,
  AVG(ratio) - (SELECT avg_ratio FROM overall_avg) AS avg_excess
FROM above_avg_patients;

assumptions.assumption: When computing the ratio, AVG(HGB) and AVG(HCT) are computed independently across all records in the Laboratory table, with SQL's AVG function ignoring NULL values. This means the ratio may be computed from different sets of records if some rows have HGB but no HCT or vice versa.

alternatives.interpretation: Only consider Laboratory records where both HGB and HCT are present (non-NULL), ensuring the ratio is always computed from a consistent set of measurements per patient.

WITH patient_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    ID,
    AVG(PIC) AS avg_pic,
    AVG(HGB) / AVG(HCT) AS ratio
  FROM Laboratory
  WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL AND HCT IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ID
),
overall_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio
  FROM patient_stats
),
above_avg_patients AS (
  SELECT avg_pic, ratio
  FROM patient_stats
  WHERE ratio > (SELECT avg_ratio FROM overall_avg)
)
SELECT 
  AVG(avg_pic) AS avg_pic,
  AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio,
  AVG(ratio) - (SELECT avg_ratio FROM overall_avg) AS avg_excess
FROM above_avg_patients;
